newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine grain harvest seen up to 26 mln T- Dep PM.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine grain harvest seen up to 26 mln T- Dep PM.

text.p: Ukraine's Deputy Prime Minister in charge of Agriculture, Mykhailo Zubets, said on Thursday that net grain output would be 26 million tonnes, up from previous forecasts of 25 million but far below last year's 36.5 million.
"A very difficult harvest year is almost finished and we will gather 26 million tonnes of grain, including grain from private farmers," Zubets told a news conference.
Zubets said Ukraine had gathered 13.1 million tonnes of winter wheat -- enough to meet domestic demand but far below last year's output of 16.4 million.
"We do not need to import any grain this year," he said. Agriculture Minister Anatoly Khorishko had earlier this month forecast a total grain harvest of 25 million tonnes.
This year's harvest is one of the worst ever for Ukraine, a one-time breadbasket among the former Soviet republics.
But Zubets said Ukraine would still export three million tonnes of grain, mostly winter wheat, from its harvest.
He said Ukraine planned to boost grain output in 1997 and to sow an extra half million hectares to winter wheat this autumn.
Winter wheat already sown was in good condition in most parts of Ukraine, he said, adding, "We are happy with developments so far."
Ukraine had so far sown 8.197 million hectares to winter wheat.
Kiev blames this year's poor harvest on severe drought conditions at the beginning of the growing season.
The government had forecast in June that output would be 36 million tonnes.
Ukraine needs about 10 million tonnes of grain a year for human and livestock consumption.
